correctness.rationale: For the stated Lebesgue-L2 projection on the open interval, Stieltjes representation gives an exact norm reduction to single jumps. Their differentiated coefficients are 2 sin(kπs) sin(kπx), k=m,3m. Absolute values have period 1/m in x. Independently, with θ=mπs and K(t)=cos(t)+cos(3t), the jump integrand after rescaling is |K(t−θ)−K(t+θ)|. On one interval of length π its integral is bounded by twice the integral of |K|, with equality at θ=π/2 modulo π by antiperiodicity. Necessity follows from the equality sign condition: translation by 2θ must preserve the zero/sign-change set of K modulo π, which is {π/4,π/2,3π/4}. Its unique gap of length π/2 forces translation by 0 modulo π; θ=0 modulo π fails the opposite-sign condition. At θ=π/2 the substitution v=cos(t) gives (2/π)∫_{−1}^1 |2−4v²| dv = (16√2−8)/(3π). The source's alternate three-region proof agrees. Direct 30,000-cell midpoint quadrature at all proposed locations for m=1,2,4 agreed to within 7.2e−8; this is a spot check, not the universal proof. No classification of arbitrary extremizing inputs is needed for the claim.
residual_risks: The quadrature does not certify the global maximum; the sign argument does.

It gives both the uniform sharp amplification and its frequency-dependent spatial witnesses; in contrast, retaining the second mode changes both the coefficient and phase.
